Broad Sept 1 risk-off (Strait of Hormuz tension, oil >$91, 10Y yields pushing toward 5%, DeepSeek reportedly developing its own AI chip) pressured the semis/AI-infra and cybersecurity complexes -- AMBER, capped as one flag, no company-specific bad news found. flags.headline: Stock fell 23% on Aug 31 -- the largest single-day decline in 25+ years -- after California's wildfire-liability reform bill died without utility protections
flags.detail: The amended bill lawmakers advanced on the final day of session omitted Gov. Newsom's proposed $6B per-incident liability cap and a subrogation ban, leaving Edison and PG&E exposed to uncapped wildfire claims tied to the January 2025 Eaton Fire under California's inverse-condemnation doctrine. EIX and PG&E together lost roughly $20B of combined market value since the prior Thursday, per the two CEOs' letter to CA legislative leaders. EIX closed Aug 31 at $54.22 (-23%) and traded +1.15% on Sept 1 to $54.55 -- a stabilization, not a recovery. Bond spreads on both utilities' debt widened on the same news.
flags.thesis_link: Directly matches two of EIX's listed key_risks: 'California's inverse condemnation doctrine holds utilities liable for wildfire damages regardless of negligence, creating a unique and structurally uninsurable business model risk that no operational improvements can fully eliminate' and 'Eaton Fire wildfire liabilities remain unresolved... which could overwhelm the California Wildfire Fund and require direct Edison liability.' This is the legislative session's binary catalyst (flagged AMBER on 2026-08-30 as '~2 weeks out') resolving against the thesis.

flags.headline: Continues sliding: -1.52% Sept 1 to $208.48, and pre-market Sept 2 quotes show a further ~3% drop toward ~$205
flags.detail: The post-Q2-earnings de-rating that began 2026-08-27/28 (underwhelming outlook despite the $12.2B Google custom-silicon deal and a revenue beat) has not stabilized -- the stock is down roughly 20% from its pre-earnings $272 high and continues to lose ground three sessions later, now compounded by the broader Sept 1 semis selloff (bond yields, DeepSeek's reported in-house AI chip effort).
flags.thesis_link: Matches MRVL's key_risk: 'Forward P/E of 50.2x... the ~20% pullback from $272 to $217 after Q2 earnings despite a revenue beat shows the market's sensitivity to execution risk, and any miss against the $16.5B FY2028 revenue target would trigger further compression.' The compression is continuing, not reversing.

flags.headline: MARA down another -3.07% Sept 1 to $10.43; no new confirmed catalyst, standing thesis risk unchanged
flags.detail: No fresh tier-1-confirmed news found for the Sept 1 move; it tracks the day's broader high-beta/crypto-adjacent softness (COIN -4.14%, ETHA -1.76%, IBIT -1.47%). Secondary-source commentary on MARA's bitcoin treasury strategy and AI-infrastructure pivot was too inconsistently dated to cite as evidence for a RED-level claim, so this flag rests on the standing thesis risk plus the persisting price trend, not a new event.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA's key_risk: 'Persistent GAAP losses... and $2.46B debt load create existential risk if bitcoin enters a prolonged downturn' and 'Revenue concentration in bitcoin mining means financial performance remains a leveraged derivative of BTC price.'
